# Miao et al. toric code artifact

`toric_32_2_H_30.alist` is copied byte-for-byte from
[`kit-cel/Quantum-Neural-BP4-demo`](https://github.com/kit-cel/Quantum-Neural-BP4-demo/tree/801ccc34a92f013422a90a421e6ad4e2149db86e/PCMs/toric_32_2),
commit `801ccc34a92f013422a90a421e6ad4e2149db86e`, path
`PCMs/toric_32_2/toric_32_2_H_30.alist` (repository MIT license).
SHA-256: `21acaad2f5307c03097b9511f9628f0e8eb8001b2a04ff6f8208ca1a0bd1814c`.

The source's Pauli labels are `I=0, X=1, Z=2, Y=3`; the local parser
converts the 15 X rows and 15 Z rows to the project's `I=0, X=1, Y=2, Z=3`
representation. The resulting CSS code has `[[32,2,4]]` parameters and
30 weight-four checks. This is the original full-rank check matrix used for
the plain BP4 comparison, not the paper's overcomplete or neural graph.

Paper: [S. Miao et al., *Quaternary Neural Belief Propagation Decoding of Quantum LDPC Codes With Overcomplete Check Matrices*, IEEE Access 13 (2025), Fig. 8](https://publikationen.bibliothek.kit.edu/1000179617/157326592).

## Independent native replay

The repository's `stabilizerCodes.cpp` is used as an independent decoder.
`native_replay.patch` adds only a setter for externally supplied errors; it
does not change the BP update or success logic. `native_replay_driver.cpp`
feeds those errors to the original flooding decoder with 25 iterations and
initialization `epsilon_0=0.1`. The local input was generated by
`prepare_native_replay.py` from the same seeded shots as the canonical run,
with a per-shot SHA-256 check before exporting.

To repeat, clone the commit above, apply `native_replay.patch` with
`git apply --unidiff-zero`, and compile from the source repository root:

```bash
g++ -std=c++17 -O3 -fopenmp -I . \
  /absolute/path/to/native_replay_driver.cpp stabilizerCodes.cpp fileReader.cpp \
  -o /tmp/bp4_miao_replay
/tmp/bp4_miao_replay < /absolute/path/to/native_input.txt > /absolute/path/to/native_raw.jsonl
```

The driver requires the original `PCMs` directory at its working directory.
The sample input and native output are retained under
`results/performance_investigation/miao_toric_d4_p0075_n10000_seed20261102/`.
`analyze_bp4_performance.py` checks the native result against every canonical
shot. The paper's plotted points are not supplied as raw counts, so the
digitized figure is treated as a qualitative check; the executable native
comparison is the direct reproducibility test.
